# lean-pkg receipt

produce lower-tier receipts (slurm, systemd: write files in the package checkout, never the registry); check a published package's receipts from git alone (check).

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg receipt [--json] COMMAND
```

## Subcommands

- [`lean-pkg receipt slurm`](#lean-pkg-receipt-slurm): a lower-tier receipt from a finished Slurm job, its verify log and its stdout seal (--template: an sbatch wrapper that meets it; --check: preflight the job's files)
- [`lean-pkg receipt systemd`](#lean-pkg-receipt-systemd): a lower-tier receipt from a finished systemd --user service unit (run bounded with --run, or its saved properties), its verify log and its stdout seal
- [`lean-pkg receipt check`](#lean-pkg-receipt-check): validate a published package's receipts from git alone: no registry, no network, never runs Lean (an outside referee's check; exit 0 only when every check passes)

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `receipt` | produce lower-tier receipts; writes files in the package checkout, never the registry. Two forms, one pipeline: `receipt slurm` (a Slurm job) and `receipt systemd` (alias `receipt local`: a systemd --user service unit). `receipt check` reads them back: a published package's receipts checked from git alone, with no registry | `slurm` `systemd` `check` |

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

## lean-pkg receipt slurm

a lower-tier receipt from a finished Slurm job, its verify log and its stdout seal (--template: an sbatch wrapper that meets it; --check: preflight the job's files).

### Usage

```text
lean-pkg receipt slurm [--job J] [--log PATH] [--receipt-commit SHA] [--template]
                       [--check] [--preflight-deps] [--deps-tar PATH] [--deps-dir DIR]
                       [--entries GLOB] [--stdout PATH] [--stderr PATH] [--redact REGEX]
                       [--sacct-file F] [--artifacts DIR] [--artifacts-manifest NAME]
                       [--checker TEXT] [--repo DIR] [--out PATH] [--compress-log]
                       [--append-readme] [--readme-heading TEXT] [--readme-line TEXT]
                       [--tar-sha256 HEX] [common flags]
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--job J` | the Slurm job id (job_id becomes slurm-J); required unless --template or --check |
| `--log PATH` | the job's raw verify log (required unless --template); when it has no `checker:` line, --checker TEXT is required |
| `--receipt-commit SHA` | the verified commit; must exist in --repo; required unless --template or --check (old spelling --commit, kept working) |
| `--template` | print a minimal sbatch wrapper whose .out/.err/log meet every check below (placeholders for the package's own commands); needs no other flag |
| `--check` | preflight the files of a finished (trial) job: every seal, stderr and log-line check, each problem named; no sacct (unless --sacct-file), commit checks only with --commit; writes nothing, exit 0/1 |
| `--preflight-deps` | before submitting: check that the staged dependency cache (--deps-tar or --deps-dir) holds, at the lake-manifest.json pins committed at --commit (default HEAD), the built .olean and .ilean of every external module in the import closure of the entry files the verifier elaborates (--entries); reads the committed tree, builds and writes nothing, exit 0/1 |
| `--deps-tar PATH` | with --preflight-deps: the DEPS_TAR tarball the job will restore (gzip, bzip2, xz or plain; read in one pass, never extracted) |
| `--deps-dir DIR` | with --preflight-deps: a directory holding .lake/packages, instead of --deps-tar |
| `--entries GLOB` | with --preflight-deps: a glob (relative to the package directory; \*\* = any directories) of the .lean files the verifier elaborates, repeatable; replaces the default Verify/\*\*/\*.lean, Audit/\*\*/\*.lean, OwnedAudit/\*\*/\*.lean, \*\*/AxiomCheck\*.lean, \*\*/TypeCheck\*.lean, \*\*/Examples\*.lean, \*\*/OwnedAudit\*.lean |
| `--stdout PATH` | the job's stdout (.out): verify-log-sha256 = sha256(raw log), pre-manifest-sha256 = post-manifest-sha256 = sha256(lake-manifest.json at the commit); without it the log must carry its own seal |
| `--stderr PATH` | the job's stderr (.err); must be empty |
| `--redact REGEX` | also replace matches with &lt;redacted&gt; (repeatable); the built-in prefixes are always redacted to &lt;USER&gt; instead (/tmp/&lt;USER&gt;-job, /scratch/&lt;USER&gt;/) |
| `--sacct-file F` | saved output of `sacct -j J --format=JobID,State,ExitCode,Elapsed,TotalCPU -P -n` (a host without Slurm) |
| `--artifacts DIR` | the collected copy of the job's sealed artifact directory (the template's ARTIFACTS_DIR): the manifest's sha256 must be the --stdout artifacts-manifest-sha256 line and every file under DIR is rehashed against it (missing, extra, changed files, symlinks, special files, path traversal and duplicate entries refuse); the receipt gains artifacts_manifest_sha256 and the manifest is written beside it. Needs --stdout |
| `--artifacts-manifest NAME` | the manifest's file name inside --artifacts DIR (default artifacts.sha256) |
| `--checker TEXT` | the exact checker command or mode (default: the log's `checker:` line) |
| `--repo DIR` | the package checkout (default: the current directory) |
| `--out PATH` | receipt path (default &lt;repo&gt;/.lean-receipts/&lt;commit12&gt;-slurm-&lt;J&gt;.json); the redacted log is written beside it as &lt;commit12&gt;-slurm-&lt;J&gt;-verify.redacted.log |
| `--compress-log` | write the redacted log as deterministic gzip &lt;...&gt;-verify.redacted.log.gz (level 9, mtime 0, no file name) instead of the plain .log; report_sha256 stays the SHA-256 of the uncompressed log and the receipt gains report_compressed {format: gzip, sha256 of the .gz, bytes uncompressed}; gate decompresses (bounded) and checks report_sha256. Restore: gzip -dc X.log.gz &gt; X.log. Without it, a log over 90 MiB prints a WARN naming this flag |
| `--append-readme` | append the entry block to README.md beside the receipt (created if absent; an entry already naming the receipt is not repeated) |
| `--readme-heading TEXT` | the entry heading after the short commit (default: lower-tier receipt, Slurm job J) |
| `--readme-line TEXT` | an extra line at the end of the entry block (repeatable) |
| `--tar-sha256 HEX` | the frozen source tarball's SHA-256, named in the entry block |

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `receipt slurm` | a lower-tier receipt from a finished Slurm job, in exactly the shape `gate --receipt` validates; reads and writes no registry. Checks, all before anything is written (every failure listed, any one refuses: exit 1, nothing written): the main job line of `sacct -j J --format=JobID,State,ExitCode,Elapsed,TotalCPU -P -n` (or `--sacct-file`, that output saved on a host with Slurm; three columns suffice; other columns need sacct's header line, which locates JobID, State and ExitCode by name, else `unexpected sacct format`) says `COMPLETED` and `0:0`; with `--stdout` (the job's `.out`) its one `verify-log-sha256` line equals the SHA-256 of the raw `--log`, and its `pre-manifest-sha256` and `post-manifest-sha256` lines are equal and equal the SHA-256 of `lake-manifest.json` committed at the commit (lines `KEY VALUE` or `KEY: VALUE`); without `--stdout`, the fallback: the log holds exactly one `verify-log-sha256: <hex>` line equal to the SHA-256 of the log without that line; `--stderr` (the `.err`), when given, is empty; `lean_toolchain` is `lean-toolchain` at the commit and `mathlib_rev` the manifest's `mathlib` rev there (else the log's `mathlib-rev:`), a disagreeing log line refuses; `sorry_count` is the log's `sorry-count:` line (never fewer than the log's `declaration uses 'sorry'` lines, else refused), else its `declaration uses 'sorry'` lines, counted only when the log shows the build finished (`Build completed successfully` or `lake build: ok`; neither a count nor a completion line refuses), and must be 0; `axioms` the log's `axioms:` line, else the union of its `#print axioms` output (neither refuses); `checker` is `--checker`, else the log's `checker:` line; optional `commit:`, `job-id:`, `generated-at:` lines must agree; a log with no `commit:` line is refused in the fallback mode (no `--stdout`), and with `--stdout` prints the stderr `WARN the verify log has no commit: line; it is bound to the commit only through lake-manifest.json` (JSON `log_commit_bound: false`; `true` with a matching line; the written receipt carries the same `log_commit_bound`, an additive key `gate` never reads, and when it is `false` the README entry gets a `- WARN:` line saying so); every field but `checker` is read from the RAW log, and a redaction that removes or alters a line the parser reads (Lean's sorry warnings, `#print axioms` output, a build-completion line, any `key:` line but `checker:`) refuses; after redacting the `/tmp/<account>-job` prefix, `/scratch/<user>/` and every `--redact` match, the public-safety scanner finds no blocking hit in the redacted log, the receipt JSON or the README entry (families listed, never the strings; besides the shared families it blocks this machine's user name and host name, full and short, at a word boundary, and a `/home/<x>` or `/Users/<x>` home directory with or without a trailing slash); a committed symlink at the commit that resolves into `.lean-receipts/` refuses (gate refuses it too); with `--append-readme`, a `README.md` that is not UTF-8 text, or a symlink, refuses before anything is written, and so does a symlinked `.lean-receipts/`. `job_id` is `slurm-<J>` (`--job` takes `J` or `slurm-J`). Writes `<c12>-slurm-<J>-verify.redacted.log` and `<c12>-slurm-<J>.json` (default `<repo>/.lean-receipts/`; `report_sha256` is the redacted log's SHA-256; a differing file already there is refused, except that a re-run differing only in a clock-stamped `generated_at` (no `generated-at:` line in the log) keeps the stored one), with `--stdout` the receipt also carries `job_stdout_sha256` and `manifest_sha256` (additive keys `gate` ignores), prints the README entry (state, exit, elapsed, TotalCPU, log name and hashes; with `--stdout` a `- Seal:` line with the job stdout and manifest SHA-256) and `next: lean-pkg gate NAME --check --receipt PATH`; `--append-readme` appends the entry to `README.md` beside the receipt (once; `--readme-heading`, `--readme-line`, `--tar-sha256` fill it; the entry's heading starts with the commit, so a `--readme-heading` that repeats this commit's SHA has it dropped). `--compress-log` writes the log as deterministic gzip `<c12>-slurm-<J>-verify.redacted.log.gz` instead (level 9, mtime 0, no file name): `report_sha256` stays the uncompressed log's SHA-256, the receipt gains the additive `report_compressed` {format: gzip, sha256 of the .gz, bytes uncompressed}, `sealed[]` lists the `.gz` (role `redacted-log.gz`, `receipt_key` `report_compressed.sha256`, `uncompressed_sha256`), restore with `gzip -dc X.log.gz > X.log` ([details](../receipts.md#a-compressed-sealed-log---compress-log)); without it a redacted log over 90 MiB prints a stderr WARN naming the flag. `--json` `{ok, receipt, log, report_sha256, raw_log_sha256, job_id, seal, log_commit_bound, report_compressed, sealed[], sacct, redactions, lines_redacted, checks[], readme_block, readme_appended, next, refusals[]}`; `sealed[]` {role, path, sha256, receipt_key} names every file the run wrote and bound (`receipt`, `redacted-log` with `report_sha256`, and for `receipt systemd` the normalised `unit.properties` with `unit_properties_sha256`), empty on a refusal: take a sidecar from it, never by its file name (`properties` in `receipt systemd`'s JSON is the raw, unsealed capture); usage errors (a missing `--log`/`--stdout`/`--stderr` file, a bad `--redact` regex) exit 2. `--template` (no other flag, no registry) prints a minimal sbatch wrapper whose `.out`, empty `.err` and log carry every line the receipt reads (the three seal lines; `checker:`, `sorry-count:`, `axioms:`, `lean-toolchain:`, `commit:`, `job-id:`, `generated-at:`), with placeholders for the package's own commands, a node-local work directory and `LEAN_NUM_THREADS` 3, and an exact-runtime preflight before any tool runs: the C locale (`LC_ALL=C LANG=C PYTHONUTF8=1`, an `#SBATCH --export` line and an `export`; stderr stays strict) and a `type -P` probe of every executable it needs, which fails the job before the work ([details](../receipts.md#a-lower-tier-receipt-from-a-slurm-job)). `--check` preflights a job's files (a short trial job before the long one): the seal, stderr, log-line, field and public-safety checks, every problem named, sacct not run (checked only from `--sacct-file` with `--job`), commit-side checks only with `--commit`; writes nothing; exit 0/1; `--json` `{ok, check, written: [], raw_log_sha256, log_commit_bound, checks[], problems[]}` (`log_commit_bound` as in a producing run, `null` without `--commit`). `--artifacts DIR` (needs `--stdout`; also with `--check`) checks the job's artifact seal (the template's optional `ARTIFACTS_DIR`): the SHA-256 of the manifest `DIR/artifacts.sha256` (`--artifacts-manifest NAME` for another name) must equal the stdout's one `artifacts-manifest-sha256` line, and every file under `DIR` is rehashed in 1 MiB chunks against it; a missing, extra or changed file, a symlink, a special file, a path-traversal, duplicate or unsorted entry refuses; the receipt gains the additive `artifacts_manifest_sha256` (`gate` ignores it), the manifest is written beside it as `<c12>-slurm-<J>-artifacts.sha256` (`sealed[]` role `artifacts.sha256`), `--json` gains `artifacts` {ok, dir, files, bytes, manifest, manifest_sha256}; without `--artifacts` nothing changes ([Recollecting a finished job](../receipts.md#recollecting-a-finished-job)). `--preflight-deps --deps-tar T` (or `--deps-dir D`, a directory holding `.lake/packages`) `[--commit SHA] [--entries GLOB]...` checks, before submitting, that the staged dependency cache holds what the verifier's own entry files need: the `import` closure of the entry files committed at `--commit` (default `HEAD`; default entries `Verify/**/*.lean`, `Audit/**/*.lean`, `OwnedAudit/**/*.lean`, `**/AxiomCheck*.lean`, `**/TypeCheck*.lean`, `**/Examples*.lean`, `**/OwnedAudit*.lean`; `--entries` replaces them) is followed through the package's committed modules and the dependencies' sources in the cache, and every external module in it needs its `.olean` and `.ilean` as regular files in exactly one manifest package (`import Mathlib` needs every module `Mathlib.lean` imports, transitively); every git package of `lake-manifest.json` must be in the cache at the manifest's `rev` (`.git/HEAD`, resolved through `refs/` or `packed-refs`); a missing module, a module no package provides (toolchain roots `Init`, `Std`, `Lean`, `Lake` aside), a module whose source is not in the cache, a missing package, a stripped or other-rev checkout, a `path` package, no entry file, or an unreadable tarball (gzip, bzip2, xz, plain) is a problem; reads only (the tarball in one pass, never extracted), builds and writes nothing; exit 0/1; `--json` `{ok, preflight_deps, commit, entries[], required_external_modules, missing_count, missing[] {module, package, files, required_by} (first 500), checks[], problems[]}`. It adds a check before submission; every check inside the job is unchanged. Details: [Receipts and trust](../receipts.md#a-lower-tier-receipt-from-a-slurm-job) | `--job J` `--log PATH` `--commit SHA` `[--stdout PATH]` `[--stderr PATH]` `[--checker TEXT]` `[--repo DIR]` `[--redact REGEX]...` `[--sacct-file F]` `[--artifacts DIR [--artifacts-manifest NAME]]` `[--out PATH]` `[--compress-log]` `[--append-readme [--readme-heading T] [--readme-line T]... [--tar-sha256 HEX]]` `[--json]`; `--template`; `--check --log PATH [--stdout PATH] [--stderr PATH] [--commit SHA] [--job J --sacct-file F] [--artifacts DIR]` |

### Exit codes

Exit 1 is also a negative answer here:

- `receipt slurm --check`: a problem with the job's files

### Examples

Print a minimal sbatch wrapper whose files pass every check; save it as verify.sbatch and edit its commands.

```bash
lean-pkg receipt slurm --template
```

Preflight the files of a finished job before writing anything; exit 1 names each problem.

```bash
lean-pkg receipt slurm --check --commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" --log verify-123.log \
  --stdout verify-123.out --stderr verify-123.err
```

Write the lower-tier receipt under .lean-receipts/ in the checkout and add its entry block to the README there.

```bash
lean-pkg receipt slurm --job 123 --commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" --log verify-123.log \
  --stdout verify-123.out --stderr verify-123.err --append-readme
```

## lean-pkg receipt systemd

a lower-tier receipt from a finished systemd --user service unit (run bounded with --run, or its saved properties), its verify log and its stdout seal.

Also spelled: `lean-pkg receipt local` ([all aliases](aliases.md)).

### Usage

```text
lean-pkg receipt systemd --unit U --log PATH --receipt-commit SHA [--stdout PATH]
                         [--stderr PATH] [--properties-file F] [--run]
                         [--memory-max BYTES] [--memory-swap-max BYTES]
                         [--cpu-quota PCT] [--runtime-max SPAN] [--setenv NAME=VALUE]
                         [--properties-out PATH] [--redact REGEX] [--checker TEXT]
                         [--repo DIR] [--out PATH] [--compress-log] [--append-readme]
                         [--readme-heading TEXT] [--readme-line TEXT] [--tar-sha256 HEX]
                         [common flags] [-- CMD ...]
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--unit U` | the service unit (`.service` added when absent); job_id becomes systemd-user:&lt;U&gt;:&lt;InvocationID&gt;@&lt;host label&gt; (h- + 12 hex of the host name's SHA-256). Required. |
| `--log PATH` | the raw verify log the unit writes; when it has no `checker:` line, --checker TEXT is required. Required. |
| `--receipt-commit SHA` | the verified commit; must exist in --repo (with --run: the checkout's clean HEAD) (old spelling --commit, kept working). Required. |
| `--stdout PATH` | the unit's stdout file: verify-log-sha256 = sha256(raw log), pre-manifest-sha256 = post-manifest-sha256 = sha256(lake-manifest.json at the commit), optional invocation-id = InvocationID; without it the log must carry its own seal. With --run the unit writes it |
| `--stderr PATH` | the unit's stderr file; must be empty. With --run the unit writes it |
| `--properties-file F` | saved `systemctl --user show U -p Id,LoadState,ActiveState,SubState,Result,InvocationID,ExecMainCode,ExecMainStatus,ExecMainStartTimestamp,ExecMainExitTimestamp,ExecMainStartTimestampMonotonic,ExecMainExitTimestampMonotonic,NRestarts,MemoryPeak,CPUUsageNSec,MemoryMax,MemorySwapMax,CPUQuotaPerSecUSec,RuntimeMaxUSec,OOMPolicy` output, captured before the unit was collected, plus a `Hostname=` line for the host it ran on |
| `--run` | start `-- CMD ...` as the bounded unit U (systemd-run --user, RemainAfterExit, WorkingDirectory=--repo), wait for it, capture its properties before stopping it; --log, --stdout, --stderr must not exist yet. The running lean-pkg's own files must not change during the run (sealed as the receipt key `producer`) |
| `--memory-max BYTES` | --run: MemoryMax (default 8G) |
| `--memory-swap-max BYTES` | --run: MemorySwapMax (default 0, so the memory cap is an OOM kill, not swapping) |
| `--cpu-quota PCT` | --run: CPUQuota (default 400%) |
| `--runtime-max SPAN` | --run: RuntimeMaxSec (default 4h) |
| `--setenv NAME=VALUE` | --run: an extra environment variable for the unit (repeatable; PATH is passed; LAKE_CACHE_DIR=&lt;fresh empty dir&gt; and LAKE_ARTIFACT_CACHE=false unless named here) |
| `--properties-out PATH` | --run: where the captured properties go (default &lt;log&gt;.unit.properties) |
| `--redact REGEX` | also replace matches with &lt;redacted&gt; (repeatable); the checkout's path, $HOME and /run/user/N/ are always redacted to &lt;repo&gt;, &lt;HOME&gt;, /run/user/&lt;UID&gt;/ instead |
| `--checker TEXT` | the exact checker command or mode (default: the log's `checker:` line) |
| `--repo DIR` | the package checkout (default: the current directory) |
| `--out PATH` | receipt path (default &lt;repo&gt;/.lean-receipts/&lt;commit12&gt;-systemd-user-&lt;U&gt;-&lt;InvocationID&gt;-&lt;host label&gt;.json); the redacted log is written beside it as &lt;commit12&gt;-systemd-user-&lt;U&gt;-&lt;InvocationID&gt;-&lt;host label&gt;-verify.redacted.log |
| `--compress-log` | write the redacted log as deterministic gzip &lt;...&gt;-verify.redacted.log.gz (level 9, mtime 0, no file name) instead of the plain .log; report_sha256 stays the SHA-256 of the uncompressed log and the receipt gains report_compressed {format: gzip, sha256 of the .gz, bytes uncompressed}; gate decompresses (bounded) and checks report_sha256. Restore: gzip -dc X.log.gz &gt; X.log. Without it, a log over 90 MiB prints a WARN naming this flag |
| `--append-readme` | append the entry block to README.md beside the receipt (created if absent; an entry already naming the receipt is not repeated) |
| `--readme-heading TEXT` | the entry heading after the short commit (default: lower-tier receipt, systemd unit U) |
| `--readme-line TEXT` | an extra line at the end of the entry block (repeatable) |
| `--tar-sha256 HEX` | the frozen source tarball's SHA-256, named in the entry block |
| `-- CMD` | with --run: the command the unit runs |

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `receipt systemd` | the same receipt from a finished systemd --user service unit, for checks run locally in a capped unit; reads and writes no registry. The unit's terminal state comes from one of: `--run -- CMD ...` (lean-pkg starts CMD as the transient unit `U` with `systemd-run --user --unit=U -p RemainAfterExit=yes -p WorkingDirectory=<repo> -p OOMPolicy=stop -p MemoryMax=8G -p MemorySwapMax=0 -p CPUQuota=400% -p RuntimeMaxSec=4h` (`--memory-max`, `--memory-swap-max`, `--cpu-quota`, `--runtime-max` change the caps; a value must be finite), the unit's stdout and stderr going to `--stdout` / `--stderr`, `PATH` and every `--setenv NAME=VALUE` passed; RemainAfterExit keeps the finished unit loaded, so lean-pkg polls `systemctl --user show U` until it is terminal, captures its properties and this host's name to `--properties-out` (default `<log>.unit.properties`, kept even when the receipt is refused) and only then stops and resets the unit; `--log`, `--stdout`, `--stderr` must not exist yet, and the checkout must be at `--commit` with no tracked change and no untracked file under the package directory before the run and still after it; untracked means listed by `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`, less `.lean-receipts/`, `.lake/` and the run's own output files; files git ignores are not checked, so they are not bound), `--properties-file F` (`systemctl --user show U -p Id,LoadState,ActiveState,SubState,Result,InvocationID,ExecMainCode,ExecMainStatus,ExecMainStartTimestamp,ExecMainExitTimestamp,ExecMainStartTimestampMonotonic,ExecMainExitTimestampMonotonic,NRestarts,MemoryPeak,CPUUsageNSec,MemoryMax,MemorySwapMax,CPUQuotaPerSecUSec,RuntimeMaxUSec,OOMPolicy` saved before the unit was collected, plus a `Hostname=` line for the host it ran on), else `systemctl --user show U` now on this host. Unit checks (every failure listed, any one refuses: exit 1, nothing written to `.lean-receipts`): `LoadState=loaded` (a `--collect` unit read after it finished is not found), `Id` is U (`.service` added), a 32-hex `InvocationID`, terminal (`ActiveState` `failed` or `inactive`, or `active` with `SubState=exited`; `activating`, `running`, `deactivating` refuse) with an exited main process, `Result=success` (`oom-kill`, `timeout`, `signal`, `core-dump`, `exit-code` are named), `ExecMainCode` exited with `ExecMainStatus` 0 (killed or dumped: the signal is named), `NRestarts` 0, a host name. Then every `receipt slurm` check: the stdout seal or the in-log fallback, an optional stdout `invocation-id` line equal to the InvocationID, an empty `--stderr`, the toolchain, Mathlib rev, sorry count, axioms, checker and the optional `commit:`, `job-id:` (the job_id or the InvocationID), `generated-at:` lines, and the public-safety scan after redacting the checkout's absolute path to `<repo>`, `$HOME` to `<HOME>`, `/run/user/N/` to `/run/user/<UID>/` and every `--redact`. `job_id` is `systemd-user:<U>:<InvocationID>@<host label>`, the label being `h-` and the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the lower-cased host name (the running system's, or the `Hostname=` line's); the host name itself is never written. Writes, beside the receipt and the redacted log, `<c12>-<slug>-unit.properties` (the recognised properties only, in a fixed order, host last as its label; its SHA-256 is the additive receipt key `unit_properties_sha256`), and prints the README entry (unit, invocation, host, Result, exit, runtime, CPU, memory peak, the caps, a `- Unit properties:` line). `--json` as `receipt slurm` with `unit` {id, invocation_id, host, active_state, sub_state, result, exec_main_code, exec_main_status, runtime_usec, cpu_usage_nsec, memory_peak, memory_max, memory_swap_max, cpu_quota_per_sec, runtime_max}, `properties` and `ran` in place of `sacct`; usage errors exit 2. A `--run` interrupted while waiting (SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP) leaves the unit running, keeps its temporary `LAKE_CACHE_DIR` while the unit may still run (removed once it is gone or finished), writes nothing, exits 128 + the signal number and prints the recovery command (the same command without `--run`) with a WARN that recovery skips the source-unchanged-during-the-run check. Details: [Receipts and trust](../receipts.md#a-lower-tier-receipt-from-a-systemd-unit) | `--unit U` `--log PATH` `--commit SHA` `[--properties-file F \| --run [--memory-max B] [--memory-swap-max B] [--cpu-quota PCT] [--runtime-max SPAN] [--setenv NAME=VALUE]... [--properties-out PATH] -- CMD ...]` `[--stdout PATH]` `[--stderr PATH]` `[--checker TEXT]` `[--repo DIR]` `[--redact REGEX]...` `[--out PATH]` `[--compress-log]` `[--append-readme [--readme-heading T] [--readme-line T]... [--tar-sha256 HEX]]` `[--json]` |
| `receipt local` | an alias of `receipt systemd`: the same flags, checks and output | as `receipt systemd` |

### Examples

Run a light verify script locally in a capped systemd --user unit and write the same lower-tier receipt as receipt slurm.

```bash
lean-pkg receipt systemd --unit audit-gate --commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" \
  --log gate/verify.log --stdout gate/unit.out --stderr gate/unit.err \
  --checker "gate.sh (lake build; #print axioms)" --run -- bash gate.sh gate/verify.log
```

## lean-pkg receipt check

validate a published package's receipts from git alone: no registry, no network, never runs Lean (an outside referee's check; exit 0 only when every check passes).

### Usage

```text
lean-pkg receipt check --repo DIR --commit SHA [--at REF] [--docs-descendants]
                       [--name NAME] [common flags]
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--repo DIR` | a local clone of the package (the package directory; cloned privately, never modified). Required. |
| `--commit SHA` | the commit the receipts bind (the page's `git checkout <commit>` line). Required. |
| `--at REF` | the published ref whose .lean-receipts/, coverage.yaml and README.md are read (default HEAD of --repo); it must be the commit or an evidence-only descendant of it |
| `--docs-descendants` | also accept a docs-only descendant (no build input changed); the author's opt-in lives in a registry the referee cannot read, so this is the referee's choice, printed in the result |
| `--name NAME` | the package name the claims must carry (default: `package` in coverage.yaml, else claims.yaml, else the directory name) |

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `receipt check` | an outside referee's check of a published package: reads no registry, opens no network connection and never runs Lean. Clones `--repo` privately (local transport only; its working tree is never read or changed), checks out the published ref (`--at`, default HEAD) and runs `gate`'s and `comparator`'s own validators on the receipts under `.lean-receipts/` that bind `--commit`: the binding (evidence-only descendants; docs-only ones too with `--docs-descendants`, the referee's choice, printed with the result), the toolchain and Mathlib pins at the commit, every SHA-256 (configurations, logs, the redacted verify log, `manifest_sha256` and the other additive evidence keys, the olean manifest record), the claims at the commit, the comparator configurations naming every reusable theorem claim, `coverage.yaml` (R11) and the README page block against the receipts. One line per check, `PASS`, `FAIL` or `SKIP` (not applicable, with the reason); `--json` lists them all. Exit 0 only when no check fails, 1 otherwise, 2 on a usage error. Re-running Lean is the comparator step of docs/trust-model.md, "Re-verify a page yourself". The 1.0 command tree's read-only verb on the `receipt` noun; the spelling `verify-receipts` is reserved for its alias table | `--repo DIR` `--commit SHA` `--at REF` `--docs-descendants` `--json` |

### Examples

In a fresh clone of a published package, check its receipts for the page's bound commit from git alone; no registry, no network, no Lean run.

```bash
lean-pkg receipt check --repo . --commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
```

Sample output:

```text
receipt check: PASS my-proof at 0123456789ab (tier comparator; 13 passed, 1 skipped)
  commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 (published ref 89abcdef0123)
  rule: evidence-only descendants (docs-only not accepted; --docs-descendants to accept them)
  ...
  PASS binding: evidence-only descendant of 0123456789ab (+3 evidence file(s))
  ...
receipt check: PASS my-proof at 0123456789ab (tier comparator; 13 passed, 1 skipped)
```

The same at a release tag, also accepting a README or notes committed after the evidence (the docs-only rule, the referee's choice); every check with its verdict as JSON.

```bash
lean-pkg receipt check --repo . --commit 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567 --at v1.0.0 --docs-descendants --json
```
